items.title: 명품 샀더니 긁히고 갈라지고··· 피해 10건 중 8건 '품질 문제'
items.summary: Korean Consumer Agency data covering 2021-August 2025 shows 674 damage-relief complaints across 13 major luxury brands, with quality issues (scratches, cracks, leather deterioration, fastener failure) accounting for 77.2% of cases. Louis Vuitton led with 175 complaints, followed by Dior (142) and Burberry (93); Gucci is named among the 13 brands examined though no brand-specific figure is broken out in the piece. Organic critical consumer-protection reporting, not Gucci-initiated.

items.title: 新浪时尚热点小时报丨2026年10月09日21时
items.summary: Sina Fashion's hourly trend roundup features Gucci resale-value discussion: overall the brand is described as not value-retentive, with secondhand prices typically 30-50% of original, while three classics (1955 Horsebit, Jackie 1961, Dionysus medium) hold 55-70%. Positions Gucci as ranked below Louis Vuitton and well behind Hermes (138% average resale appreciation) in a peer comparison, a mildly critical framing on durability of value versus competitors.

items.title: Gucci涨价规律揭秘：为什么2026年畅销款反而降价近30%？
items.summary: Weibo post argues Gucci's ~30% official price cut on the Ophidia mini bucket bag (12,300 to 8,700 yuan) is not a consumer win but merely the counter price catching up to secondary-market levels already around 6,000 yuan, attributing the move to slowing luxury demand forcing inventory clearance. Concludes the era of buying Gucci bags as a financial asset has ended. Organic skeptical consumer-finance commentary, not brand-sourced.

items.title: 古驰国内国外价差还有多少？2026年大降价后已不足10%
items.summary: Weibo FAQ-style post reports Gucci's mainland China vs Europe price gap has narrowed from a historical 30-50% to under 10% following the September 2026 markdowns (Ophidia mini bucket 40%+ cut, GG Marmont small bucket to 8,100 yuan). Links the move to H1 2026 comparable revenue down 5% and Asia-Pacific down 10%, quoting Kering leadership that the industry's pricing power has eroded. Frames the cut as a defensive response to weak results rather than a goodwill gesture.

items.title: 看了十分钟就买了，8200买的古驰鞋破损顾客质疑质量
items.summary: Consumer-complaint report: a customer who bought Gucci shoes for 8,200 yuan at a Hangzhou counter found the shoes damaged shortly after purchase and is disputing quality with the retailer. A companion case cited elsewhere in the same consumer-complaint cycle involves a ~15,000 yuan Gucci bag from a Guangzhou counter where a quality defect found on day one was refused refund/return. Organic quality-control grievance coverage, included despite being past the ideal 7-day freshness band because it is directly corroborated by today's Seoul Finance quality-complaint story, giving converging signal on the same theme across markets.

items.source: Yahoo! Japan News (newscafe/モデルプレス syndication)
items.title: 山田涼介・戸田恵梨香、銀座で開催のグッチイベントに来場 ブランドの新たな世界観を堪能
items.summary: Gucci staged an exclusive invitation event, 'The World of Exclusive Creations,' in Ginza, Tokyo, displaying rare handbags, leather goods, eveningwear and high jewelry curated by artistic director Demna, with a tapestry installation echoing the Milan 'Gucci Memoria' exhibition. Brand ambassador Toda Erika and Friend-of-the-House Yamada Ryosuke (Hey! Say! JUMP) attended. Purely descriptive activation coverage with no independent evaluative verdict from the outlet; tagged activation_coverage.

items.title: 싱글벙글 명품 브랜드 구찌 근황
items.summary: Korean community best-board thread discussing Gucci's current state, circulating within the 명품(luxury) gallery and promoted to the dcbest real-time best board. Thread format (meme/screenshot roundup of Gucci's recent business and design struggles) typical of DCInside's informal, often sardonic brand commentary; reflects organic community chatter rather than press coverage. Specific like/reply counts not exposed via fetch.

items.title: Has Gucci proved Made in China has a long way to go?
items.summary: Critical trade-press analysis polling fashion-industry professionals on perceptions of Chinese manufacturing quality following Gucci's Made in China Drip sneaker. Argues the launch may have reinforced rather than resolved consumer skepticism about Chinese-made luxury goods, with a persistent perception gap remaining between improving manufacturing capability and brand-origin prestige that Gucci's own move may have exposed rather than closed. Independent critical judgment, not brand-sourced.
